mbm-1626.clue: I carry a spare page for the marmot.
mbm-1626.quote: On the trail I stopped to sketch a marmot. It sat on my open notebook instead. I drew the view on the back of a receipt and kept the dusty pawprints as page one.

mbm-1627.clue: I carry a picture of a perfectly empty freezer.
mbm-1627.quote: Dad ran an ice-cream van for thirty years. On his last day I photographed him reflected in the shiny bottom of the empty tub. You can see the pink roof in his glasses.

mbm-1628.clue: I ask for both socks in different colors.
mbm-1628.quote: My sister cheers from a new corner on every lap. I wear one violet sock and one lime one so she can tell which leg is winning. She takes this very seriously.

mbm-1629.clue: My lunch goes downhill before I do.
mbm-1629.quote: My first solo run began when a clementine slipped out of my pocket. I watched it bounce down the beginner slope and skied after it. At the bottom a ski instructor handed me my breakfast.

mbm-1630.clue: My board game has a working drawbridge.
mbm-1630.quote: The cardboard bridge fell down every time the dragon crossed. I hinged it with two bits of ribbon from my daughter's hair. She named herself Keeper of the Bridge and charges buttons.

mbm-1631.clue: I set one place with a chipped green plate.
mbm-1631.quote: My uncle taught me to pat arepas between my palms over that plate. I still get flour on the green rim. The first one off the griddle goes to him, even if he's the last one through the door.

mbm-1632.clue: I've got a running partner who never leaves the block.
mbm-1632.quote: On my route a shopkeeper moves a toy runner one shelf higher each time I pass. When I make it to the fifth shelf she opens the door and rings her bicycle bell.

mbm-1633.clue: I buy my popcorn after the picture.
mbm-1633.quote: I started going to the final matinee with my grandma when she worked the concession stand. She saves the last little striped carton for our walk home. We review the movie one kernel at a time.

mbm-1634.clue: There are four clouds in my pencil case.
mbm-1634.quote: Our anime club tried drawing the same scene from four different seats. We pinned our sketches together and the cloud kept drifting across the page. I drew a kite to chase it.

mbm-1635.clue: I borrowed a mirror for the group photo.
mbm-1635.quote: I was always the missing cousin in the pictures. This year I propped a hand mirror by the croquet set so my face would appear in the corner. Dad wore his best tie for the mirror.

mbm-1636.clue: I keep a chair empty at the card table.
mbm-1636.quote: My best card is a snail knight who takes three turns to arrive. When I play him I set his card on the empty chair. My opponents have started offering him refreshments on the way.

mbm-1637.clue: I play hide-and-seek with the yellow roof.
mbm-1637.quote: Paddling the estuary, I can see our yellow shed through one gap in the reeds. I lifted my paddle in a wave and the laundry on the line flapped back. Close enough.

mbm-1638.clue: I put one square in the post every winter.
mbm-1638.quote: My sister and I swap quilt squares by mail. Last time the envelope had a round coffee stain. I traced it in brown thread and put a tiny saucer underneath.

mbm-1639.clue: I make a flipbook of mistakes.
mbm-1639.quote: Every time somebody in anime club draws a lopsided robot, I save it. Fanned together they make the robot look as though it's doing a wobbly dance. We voted it into the show.

mbm-1640.clue: My aerial wears a little yellow bow.
mbm-1640.quote: The radio club helped me string an antenna past our lemon tree. On my first distant call a lemon rolled straight onto my logbook. I mailed the other operator a drawing of its perfect circle.

mbm-1641.clue: I keep one black bishop under the picnic table.
mbm-1641.quote: The first rain during park chess caught us halfway through a game. My opponent chalked the positions underneath the table. We came back in the sun, ducked our heads, and finished.

mbm-1642.clue: I drew a little moon on the tuning knob.
mbm-1642.quote: The first late-night voice I caught on my radio was a baker waiting for his dough to rise. He described the moon through his window and I sketched mine beside the dial.

mbm-1643.clue: The orange square has two birthdays.
mbm-1643.quote: I made my nephew a quilt from his old birthday shirts. He wore the same orange dinosaur two years running, so I cut two tiny party hats and stitched them both to the square.

mbm-1644.clue: I spent my whole allowance on one handle.
mbm-1644.quote: I found a silver-handled umbrella at the flea market with no fabric left on it. My mum and I sewed on a red canopy. Now I hope it'll rain on shopping day.

mbm-1645.clue: My model has better table manners than I do.
mbm-1645.quote: I bent a tiny spoon for my robot cook and made a soup pot out of a bottle top. My brother asked why a robot needed lunch. I pointed to the little chairs waiting at the counter.

mbm-1646.clue: You'll know my corner by the brass fish.
mbm-1646.quote: A bronze fish is set into the square by my favorite park chess table. My opponent sets our clock beside its nose. When I'm short on time it looks as if the fish is counting down.

mbm-1647.clue: I quilt the darkness in three colors.
mbm-1647.quote: My brother thinks our hometown sky is black. I stitched it in navy, plum and charcoal, then showed him the quilt at dusk. He picked the very minute the three colors matched.

mbm-1648.clue: I can hear the lap before I see it.
mbm-1648.quote: My dad whistles our family tune when I get to the wall. Last week his whistle cracked halfway through. I knew it was him even better and missed my turn laughing.

mbm-1649.clue: I keep a tiny chair drawn beside one tune.
mbm-1649.quote: At my first trad session I only knew the first part of the reel. A fiddler tapped the empty chair with her foot and played the B part slowly. I drew the chair in my notebook.

mbm-1650.clue: My lifting log has a flap over one number.
mbm-1650.quote: I promised my training partner I wouldn't peek at the week's target. She wrote it under a folded paper flap and painted a little mountain on top. We open the mountain after the last set.
